papers.title: Acoustic-phonon-driven spin-lattice relaxation of the hBN boron vacancy in the sub-THz regime
papers.authors: Priyo Adhikary, Pramey Upadhyaya
papers.summary: First-principles modeling of a boron-vacancy center in hBN includes finite-momentum acoustic phonons. It identifies resonant one-phonon processes and flexural modes as important high-field relaxation channels.
papers.whyRelevant: An adjacent defect platform that tests the limits of models restricted to zone-center optical modes.

relatedPapers.reason: Both examine which phonon modes control spin–lattice relaxation.

papers.title: Ultrafast Core–Shell Spin Transfer and Spin-Selective Relaxation in an Endohedral Cage Cluster
papers.authors: Xueke Yu, Qi Gao, Yu Chen, Wei Pei, Xiuyun Zhang, Yan Su, Jijun Zhao
papers.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.summary: Real-time electronic-structure simulations follow laser-driven spin redistribution between a manganese center and its tin cage. The calculated early dynamics and relaxation channels distinguish spin-conserving processes from slower spin-flip pathways.
papers.whyRelevant: A molecular-cluster case study for separating optical spin transfer from subsequent relaxation.

relatedPapers.reason: Both examine localized spins in molecular cage or cluster environments.

papers.title: Electron-Phonon Coupling with Spin and Orbital Angular Momentum Transfer
papers.authors: Mengxiang Xie, Jie Ren
papers.summary: A microscopic theory extends electron–phonon angular-momentum coupling to include both spin and orbital contributions. It connects local lattice motion with continuum rotation descriptions and identifies effects beyond long-wavelength approximations.
papers.whyRelevant: Provides theoretical context for deciding which vibrational couplings a molecular-spin relaxation model should retain.

relatedPapers.reason: Both study microscopic links between lattice vibrations and spin behavior.

papers.title: Relaxation dynamics in strongly coupled spin systems in zero- to ultralow-field NMR spectroscopy
papers.authors: Florin Teleanu, Anne M. Fabricant, Chengtong Zhang, Gary P. Centers, Dmitry Budker, Danila A. Barskiy, Alexej Jerschow
papers.summary: Zero-to-ultralow-field NMR experiments and relaxation modeling reveal multiple decay times in strongly coupled nuclear spins. Shuttling, measurement field and excitation angle change individual spectral components and their lifetimes.
papers.whyRelevant: Shows how preparation and control choices affect the interpretation of measured relaxation.

relatedPapers.reason: Both emphasize dynamical modeling rather than assigning every decay to a single relaxation constant.

papers.title: Line-narrowing by polychromatic selective spin-locking in NMR
papers.authors: Coline Wiame, Hadi Loutfi, Kirill Sheberstov, Geoffrey Bodenhausen
papers.summary: Selective radio-frequency spin locking narrows NMR lines while decoupling scalar interactions. The approach can enhance signals in conventional relaxation measurements and experiments involving long-lived spin states.
papers.whyRelevant: A pulse-method reference for separating inhomogeneous broadening from relaxation-limited linewidths.

relatedPapers.reason: Both rely on selective control of spin transitions, although in different resonance regimes.

papers.title: Complete coherent control of spin qubits in self-assembled InAs quantum dots under oblique magnetic fields
papers.authors: I Samaras, K Barr, C Schneider, S Höfling, K G Lagoudakis
papers.summary: An InAs quantum-dot experiment demonstrates Rabi oscillations, Ramsey fringes and arbitrary spin rotations under an oblique magnetic field. Field orientation tunes the spin-state mixing and optical coupling rather than merely imposing an alignment constraint.
papers.whyRelevant: An adjacent spin-control platform suggesting how orientation can become a useful control parameter.

relatedPapers.reason: Both demonstrate coherent electron-spin addressing, with different host systems.

papers.title: Rare-Event Quantum Sensing Using Logical Qubits
papers.authors: Robert Ott, Torsten V. Zache, Soonwon Choi, Adam M. Kaufman, Hannes Pichler
papers.summary: A theoretical rare-event sensing protocol uses error-correction syndrome extraction to distinguish signal and noise through higher-order correlations. It trades reduced logical signal strength for longer acquisition coherence under local Markovian noise.
papers.whyRelevant: Provides a conceptual comparison between preserving coherence and retaining the particular signal a sensor must measure.

relatedPapers.reason: Both consider how error-handling protocols affect useful quantum operations.

papers.title: Quantum-enhanced sensing of molecular excited-state dynamics with correlated photons
papers.authors: Jiahao Joel Fan, Feihong Liu, Dangyuan Lei, Shaul Mukamel, Zhedong Zhang
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
papers.summary: A microscopic pump–probe theory uses correlated squeezed photons to improve access to molecular excited-state dynamics. A semiconductor model illustrates selective signals and shows why intermediate squeezing can be preferable to stronger squeezing.
papers.whyRelevant: Connects optical quantum correlations to the problem of isolating molecular dynamical pathways.

relatedPapers.reason: Both involve optical access to quantum states, although the readout mechanisms differ.

papers.title: Quantum metrology of spin sensing with free space electrons
papers.authors: Santiago Beltràn-Romero, Michael Gaida, Philipp Haslinger, Dennis Raetzel, Stefan Nimmrichter
papers.summary: A scattering model evaluates the precision limits of probing localized magnetic moments with free electrons. It compares conventional imaging with alternative electron measurements and identifies when spin backaction changes the optimal readout.
papers.whyRelevant: An adjacent sensing platform that makes the role of measurement backaction explicit.

relatedPapers.reason: Both relate probe dynamics to information about a microscopic spin environment.

papers.title: Enhanced room-temperature spin transport in a deuterated molecular single crystal
papers.authors: Tingting Yang, Cheng Zhang, Yang Qin, Meng Wu, Mingyi Ding, Zirui Wang, Lidan Guo, Xianrong Gu, Ke Meng, Shunhua Hu, Ruiheng Zheng, Yong Wang, Min Li, Xiangpeng Zhang, Rui Zhang, Qiong Zhou, Lingyun Zhu, Zhixiang Wei, Xiangnan Sun
papers.summary: A deuterated molecular single crystal combines suppressed spin-relaxation channels with an electrode-transfer process designed to avoid crystal damage. Experiments and calculations support improved room-temperature spin transport in the resulting devices.
papers.whyRelevant: Closely connects isotope engineering, spin lifetime and gentle single-crystal fabrication.

relatedPapers.reason: Both emphasize preserving fragile crystals and controlling contacts during device fabrication.

papers.title: Organic Semiconductor Single Crystals: From Continuous Fabrication to Optoelectronic Applications
papers.authors: Zhixiang Zhong, Jie Ren, Hanying Li
papers.summary: A review of organic semiconductor single crystals links crystallization kinetics and continuous fabrication to carrier transport and optoelectronic devices. It identifies processing and contact-compatible device fabrication as continuing challenges.
papers.whyRelevant: Provides broader context for scaling experiments from individual high-quality crystals to device platforms.

relatedPapers.reason: Both concern fabricating devices while preserving the advantages of molecular single crystals.

papers.title: Assembling Polyhedral Metal–Organic Framework Superstructures by Bidirectional Shear
papers.authors: Wenrui Li, Zinan Huang, Zihan Xu, Zhen Hu, Junsong Wu, Lianbin Zhang, Jintao Zhu
papers.summary: Alternating shear organizes polyhedral ZIF-8 particles into large-area ordered composite structures. Dynamic interactions in the polymer matrix coordinate both particle orientation and positional order.
papers.whyRelevant: A processing example for extending structural control from individual framework particles to larger assemblies.

relatedPapers.reason: Both address how assembly order determines functional material structure.

papers.title: Pressure-Driven Cooperative Intermolecular–Covalent Bond Relaxation in a Hydrogen-Bonded Organic Framework
papers.authors: Yong Zhou, Hengxin Fang, Aiping Yang, Zhaoyang Zheng, Changqing Sun
papers.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.summary: High-pressure Raman measurements and calculations resolve how a hydrogen-bonded framework redistributes compression between intermolecular contacts and covalent bonds. Opposite vibrational shifts support a cooperative local-bond adjustment mechanism.
papers.whyRelevant: A structural-dynamics comparison for relating framework rigidity to specific vibrational coordinates.

relatedPapers.reason: Both motivate mode-resolved analysis of molecular-framework dynamics.

papers.title: Three-Dimensional Covalent Organic Framework for the Capture of Nitrogen Dioxide
papers.authors: Thien D. Duong, Siyu Zhou, Xin Lian, Zhaozhao Hu, Yuhang Yang, Zi Wang, Ran Eitan Abutbul, Joseph Hurd, Shubha S. Gunaga, Frédéric Mentink-Vigier, Daniel Lee, Jiangnan Li, Sihai Yang
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: A three-dimensional COF is built from a twisted biphenyl aldehyde and characterized using diffraction, hyperpolarized NMR and modeling. The work identifies interpenetration and missing-linker-related sites that contribute to gas binding.
papers.whyRelevant: A synthesis and characterization example for treating defects as structural features rather than assuming an ideal framework.

relatedPapers.reason: Both require relating synthetic conditions to actual framework structure.

papers.title: Electron-electron interactions mediated by overdamped vibrations: Implications for chirality-induced spin selectivity
papers.authors: Leonardo Celada, Rocco Bellusci, D. K. Andrea Phan-Huu, Alessandro Chiesa, Stefano Carretta
papers.summary: A theoretical molecular-bridge model shows how rapidly damped vibrations can mediate spin-dependent electronic interactions. Simulated transfer develops spin polarization under specified local-loss assumptions, with coherent and dissipative effects both contributing.
papers.whyRelevant: Relevant to chiral molecular qubits and spin–vibration coupling; the model does not establish a universal explanation of CISS.

relatedPapers.reason: Relevant to chiral molecular qubits and spin–vibration coupling; the model does not establish a universal explanation of CISS.

papers.title: High Proton Conduction in a Hydrogen-Bonded Co(II) Framework through Pendant Carboxylic Acid-Decorated 1D Channels
papers.authors: Rudra Chand, Maniprakundil Neeshma, Punnappadam Rajan Suraj, SantoshKumar D Bhat, Subhadip Neogi
papers.summary: A cobalt framework with accessible carboxylic-acid groups forms humidity-dependent proton-conduction pathways. Comparison with a related framework lacking those groups highlights the combined roles of channel chemistry and confined water.
papers.whyRelevant: Useful for distinguishing protonic and electronic transport in moisture-responsive conductive frameworks.

relatedPapers.reason: Useful for distinguishing protonic and electronic transport in moisture-responsive conductive frameworks.

papers.title: Ultrasound-Assisted Facile Nanoconfinement of Luminescent Guests in Zirconium Metal-Organic Frameworks
papers.authors: Yiyi Wang, James D. Taylor, Jin-Chong Tan
papers.summary: Probe ultrasonication accelerates the preparation of zirconium MOF nanocrystals and the encapsulation of fluorescent guests. Structural and photophysical characterization connects the preparation conditions and host–guest environment with emission behavior.
papers.whyRelevant: A transferable host–guest synthesis approach for functional frameworks; luminescence is demonstrated, not qubit coherence.

relatedPapers.reason: A transferable host–guest synthesis approach for functional frameworks; luminescence is demonstrated, not qubit coherence.

papers.title: A rhombic spin-1 interpretation of a room-temperature GaN emitter
papers.authors: Daniel Hashemi
papers.summary: A rhombic spin-1 model is tested against room-temperature ODMR lines from a GaN defect. It reproduces several line positions, but the available data do not uniquely establish the assignment; a zero-field measurement is proposed to distinguish competing interpretations.
papers.whyRelevant: Offers a careful example of spin-Hamiltonian identification and uncertainty assessment relevant to characterizing new molecular qubits.

relatedPapers.reason: Offers a careful example of spin-Hamiltonian identification and uncertainty assessment relevant to characterizing new molecular qubits.

papers.title: Emergence of Chern metal in a moiré Kondo lattice
papers.authors: Wenjin Zhao, Zui Tao, Yichi Zhang, Bowen Shen, Zhongdong Han, Patrick Knüppel, Yihang Zeng, Zhengchao Xia, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Jie Shan, Kin Fai Mak
papers.summary: Transport and magnetic measurements identify a compressible state with chiral edge transport near magnetic Kondo breakdown in a moiré bilayer. The results link band topology and correlated magnetism in a tunable two-dimensional system.
papers.whyRelevant: An adjacent emergent-physics reference for correlated electronic materials; the demonstrated material is not a MOF.

relatedPapers.reason: An adjacent emergent-physics reference for correlated electronic materials; the demonstrated material is not a MOF.

papers.title: Detection and Inhibition of Decoherence Through Collisions: A dynamical approach
papers.authors: Sagnik Chakraborty, Srijon Ghosh, Federico Amato, Gniewomir Sarbicki, Dariusz Chruściński, Rosario Lo Franco
papers.summary: The authors propose collision-model protocols for protecting physical and logical qubit states without complete prior knowledge of the noise. The work develops a theoretical approach to state preservation rather than reporting a molecular-spin experiment.
papers.whyRelevant: Provides an adjacent noise-protection concept to compare with dynamical-decoupling-based error mitigation.

relatedPapers.reason: Provides an adjacent noise-protection concept to compare with dynamical-decoupling-based error mitigation.

papers.title: Redox-Active Spin Trapping for the Electrochemical Detection, Quantification, and Kinetic Analysis of Sulfate Radicals in Aqueous Media
papers.authors: Seth T. Putnam, Zirui Wang, Collin Reutimann, Joaquín Rodríguez-López
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.archiveJournal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: Electrochemical detection captures unstable sulfate-radical spin-trap adducts before they decay in water. Combined EC-EPR, microelectrode measurements and simulations enable quantification and kinetic analysis while addressing a source of conventional spin-trapping misassignment.
papers.whyRelevant: A useful chemical-sensing reference on transient species and measurement artifacts; it is not coherent quantum sensing.

relatedPapers.reason: A useful chemical-sensing reference on transient species and measurement artifacts; it is not coherent quantum sensing.

papers.title: Chirality-Induced Spin Selectivity in Photoinduced Charge-Separations of Cryptochrome: Potential Role in Magnetoreception
papers.authors: Yasuhiro Kobori, Misato Hamada, Tatsuya Iwata, Hiroki Nagashima, Masaaki Fuki, Hideki Kandori, Stefan Weber
papers.journal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.archiveJournal: The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
papers.summary: Time-resolved EPR measures a modest chirality-associated contribution to polarization in cryptochrome charge-separated states. Model calculations explore how such polarization could influence radical-pair directional sensitivity; the biological implication remains a proposed mechanism.
papers.whyRelevant: Connects molecular chirality, spin-selective charge transfer and magnetic sensing.

relatedPapers.reason: Connects molecular chirality, spin-selective charge transfer and magnetic sensing.

papers.title: Precise modular engineering of neutral organometallic rectangles from binuclear palladacycles via hierarchical assembly strategy
papers.authors: Yanzhe Ma, Lixin Duan, Tianheng Hou, Jiaxin Zhang, Haonan Sun, Ran Ma, Tao Tu
papers.summary: A hierarchical assembly route separates geometric programming from the final locking of neutral palladium-based rectangles. Structural characterization shows size control and guest-dependent deformation without breaking the established metal–carbon framework connectivity.
papers.whyRelevant: Provides an adjacent coordination-assembly strategy for balancing structural correction, robustness and guest response.

relatedPapers.reason: Provides an adjacent coordination-assembly strategy for balancing structural correction, robustness and guest response.

papers.title: Protein Scaffolds Modulate the Electronic Structure of a Common Ketyl Radical Intermediate in Thiamine Pyrophosphate-Dependent Radical Biocatalysis: Insights from EPR and ENDOR Spectroscopy
papers.authors: Guodong Rao, Zheng Zhang, Xin Liu, Angela A. Shiau, R. David Britt, Yang Yang
papers.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.archiveJournal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.summary: Multifrequency EPR, ENDOR and calculations identify enzyme-bound ketyl radicals and resolve how different protein environments redistribute their spin density. Hyperfine measurements connect a chemically identical radical intermediate with different local electronic structures.
papers.whyRelevant: The transferable element is hyperfine-resolved radical characterization, rather than the biocatalytic application.

relatedPapers.reason: The transferable element is hyperfine-resolved radical characterization, rather than the biocatalytic application.

papers.title: Electric field–controlled spin transport in a topological insulator interfaced with a ferroelectric antiferromagnet
papers.authors: Yogesh Kumar, Pushpendra Gupta, Xinyan Li, Richa Mudgal, Ashish Omar, Ryan Chen, Mito Funatsu, Maya Ramesh, Nicholas Reiterer, Yuanqi Lyu, Yiping Zeng, Darrell G. Schlom, Alessandra Lanzara, Robert J. Birgeneau, James G. Analytis, Ramamoorthy Ramesh, Sajid Husain
papers.summary: Nonlocal transport measurements examine spin–charge conversion across a topological-insulator and multiferroic interface. Thickness dependence identifies the role of decoupled surface states, alongside electric-field control in the hybrid device.
papers.whyRelevant: A comparative example of interface-controlled spin transport for the materials and devices direction.

relatedPapers.reason: A comparative example of interface-controlled spin transport for the materials and devices direction.
